life_summary: Delbert Llewellyn Stapley was born on December 11, 1896, in Mesa, Arizona Territory, during the early days of Arizona settlement. He grew up in the Arizona LDS community and received his education in territorial schools. Stapley developed a strong commitment to community service and religious duty from an early age. During World War I, he served with distinction in the U.S. Marine Corps, demonstrating patriotic commitment alongside his religious convictions. Despite being offered a contract with Major League Baseball, Stapley declined to pursue missionary service, prioritizing his religious calling over professional sports opportunity. He established a family and business interests in Arizona while maintaining deep roots in the local LDS community where he had grown up.
church_summary: Stapley served as a missionary in the Southern States Mission from 1915 to 1917. He was ordained as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles on October 5, 1950, and served in that capacity until his death on August 19, 1978. Throughout his apostolic career, Stapley was active in youth programs, receiving the Silver Buffalo Award from the Boy Scouts in 1969 for distinguished service. He was instrumental in organizing the original Miami Stake in 1961, bringing Church structure to rapidly growing communities in Florida. His service as an apostle spanned nearly three decades of significant growth and expansion in the Church.
